metadata.title: Exact minimum size on the first interior shell of the Bougard-Joret problem, with the extremal graphs at independence numbers two and k-1
metadata.description: Let f(n,α,k) be the minimum size of a k-connected graph of order n and independence number α. Bougard and Joret conjectured a two-line formula for f, and Das and Gupta determined the boundary n=α+k and disproved the first line there. We determine f on the entire first interior shell n=α+k+1: f(α+k+1,α,k)=⌈ k(α+k+1)/2⌉ for every k≥3 and 2≤α≤ k+1, the degree-sum bound. The extremal graphs combine a Harary-type residual graph of order k+1, a cycle power with a complement matching, with an independent set joined through distinct missing-neighbor pairs; an elementary cyclic-gap argument gives connectivity in every parity case. For α=2 the extremizers are exactly the complements of disjoint unions of cycles of length at least five. For α=k-1 they are exactly the graphs built on a nonstar tree with prescribed fibers, so f(2k,k-1,k)=k², one more than the boundary value k²-1. Exact computations test the proofs: the 75 constructions with 3≤ k≤12 are rebuilt by a second implementation, 75 damaged-edge and 8 complement-cycle controls behave as predicted, and labeled enumerations for k≤5 and a census of all 32,768 graphs on six vertices agree with the theorems. The universal statements rest on the proofs, not on the finite computations. The values of f beyond the shell are not determined here.
metadata.version_notes: Adds a related-work section (the proved cases of Bougard and Joret, the boundary theorem, the second line, the next-matching value), a section of algorithms with their costs, and a results section with the 75 shell constructions, the negative controls, the labeled residual enumeration and an ablation, with tables and figures generated by make_tables.py from the saved certificates. The shell parameter g = k - a replaces d, and the proof states the requirement m >= 2r + 4 of the cyclic-gap lemma. The statements and proofs of the three theorems are unchanged. The title is re-derived from the theorems.
